repos.name: advent
repos.title: advent · Advent of Code in Haskell, 2015–2025
repos.description: Haskell solutions to every Advent of Code puzzle from 2015 to 2025, one file per day, in a viewer that shows each solution next to a short critique of how it works and where it is weak, from plain Haskell in 2015 to the quaalude custom prelude in 2025.

repos.name: agent-utils
repos.title: Agent Utils · the toolbox around a coding agent
repos.description: Agent Utils is a Pi package and a set of standalone tools that give coding agents a voice, eyes, hands and a fleet: speech in and out, images and screens, choices, session control, work apps and fleet-wide dashboards.

repos.name: aish
repos.title: aish — a terminal you can talk to
repos.description: aish is an audio-first conversational terminal: a real persistent shell and a persistent agent in one transcript, fully usable with the screen off.

repos.name: android-utils
repos.title: android-utils
repos.description: android-utils: Linux desktops, a terminal, a floating window manager and more for Android — built with Nix, shipped through Google Play internal testing.

repos.name: annum
repos.title: Annum — Calendar, mail & Teams
repos.description: Annum brings your Microsoft 365 calendar, mail and Teams conversations into a native workspace for Mac and Android.

repos.name: cacophony
repos.title: Cacophony — conduct a swarm of coding agents
repos.description: Cacophony runs a coordinated swarm of coding agents for every repository: one task board, one message bus and one lifecycle controller across all of your machines.

repos.name: caravan
repos.title: Caravan — A merge queue that keeps agents moving
repos.description: Caravan is a deterministic, agent-friendly merge queue built directly on GitHub pull-request topology—no queue database required.

repos.name: collective
repos.title: Collective · one Nix flake for every machine
repos.description: Collective is one typed Nix flake that configures a fleet of NixOS desktops and servers, WSL devboxes, a Mac and its Linux VM, and Android phones: one registry, one module tree, prebuilt closures and a CLI to run it.

repos.name: cost
repos.title: Cost — AI credit usage
repos.description: AI credit usage, rolling spend rate and reset-aware history. Cost for macOS, Android and the terminal.

repos.name: crossbow
repos.title: Crossbow · a pipeline language for solving puzzles
repos.description: Crossbow is a small, dynamically typed programming language written in Haskell for solving puzzles interactively: values flow through pipelines of curried functions, lists of functions apply element-wise, and its standard library is written in Crossbow. How it reads and runs, with output from the real interpreter.

repos.name: ctx
repos.title: ctx · shared, versioned, watchable context for agents and programs
repos.description: ctx is one small daemon that keeps a versioned JSON tree for every agent, session and script: read it, write it with compare-and-set, watch it change, put it in prompts and wake agents when it moves.

repos.name: io-mcp
repos.title: io-mcp — MCP hub for agent–human communication
repos.description: A centralised MCP server that connects AI coding agents to humans through TTS, choices, messaging, and terminal graphics. Run a whole project from your phone with a scroll wheel and earphones — or from any terminal.

repos.name: kittui
repos.title: kittui · terminal graphics, natively
repos.description: kittui renders graphics into the terminal through the kitty graphics protocol, from Rust, C, TypeScript, Python or the shell, and kittwm composes terminals, browsers and native windows into one window manager.

repos.name: mcp-cli
repos.title: mcp-cli · Rust crates for CLIs that are also MCP servers
repos.description: mcp-cli-core runs one typed Rust command as a CLI with JSON output or as a tool on an MCP stdio server. Four companion crates add configuration, self-update, feedback reporting and a cache-and-daemon transport. How they work, a recorded MCP session, and their tests.

repos.name: nix-reflect
repos.title: nix-reflect · a Nix parser and evaluator written in Nix
repos.description: nix-reflect is a Nix library that parses Nix source into an inspectable tree and evaluates that tree to a value, with scopes, lazy thunks and typed errors implemented in Nix itself. How it works, and how much of the language it handles today, measured against the real evaluator.

repos.name: nlir
repos.title: nlir — natural-language IR
repos.description: A small language for programs over data and meaning: exact structure and model-realised semantics in one evaluator — forwards and backwards.

repos.name: omni-cli
repos.title: omni · cast keystrokes to every device
repos.description: omni casts keystrokes, text, key combos and scrolls from one CLI to the omni keyboard on Android, iOS and watches, to desktops through a replay daemon, and to agents over MCP, using one NDJSON wire.

repos.name: owt
repos.title: owt · a server whose endpoints arrive with the request
repos.description: owt is a small Flask server that runs the Python code each request carries and returns the result, so any language that can make an HTTP request can call a Python library without a new endpoint being written. How it works, its pipe syntax, and its sharp edges, shown with requests to a local server.

repos.name: panopticon
repos.title: Panopticon — your desktop, zoomed out into an agent's instrument
repos.description: Panopticon is a macOS overlay that zooms the live desktop out into a CRT-styled pi agent harness. The agent sees the screen, rewinds it, and drives it — while you watch every action.

repos.name: paratenic
repos.title: Paratenic — host the agents you already run
repos.description: Paratenic is an Agent Host Protocol server for live agent sessions: it adopts Pi sessions already running, starts Pi agents for sessions clients create, and serves them to every AHP client.

repos.name: pi-daemon
repos.title: pi-daemon — the Pi Durable agent host
repos.description: pi-daemon runs Pi agents as Durable sessions: one SQLite store per session, crash-only workers, and AHP, ACP and Chord for Culture, editors and applications. Kill it mid-turn; nothing is lost and nothing runs twice.

repos.name: pulseaudio-lambda
repos.title: pulseaudio-lambda · live audio through any command
repos.description: pulseaudio-lambda records audio from PulseAudio, pipes it through any command's stdin and stdout, and plays the result, so a filter can be a shell script, a sox effect or a Python model. Its main use is a streaming stem separator that removes the drums from whatever is playing. How the bridge works and how much latency it adds, measured.

repos.name: quaalude
repos.title: quaalude · a custom Haskell prelude for Advent of Code
repos.description: quaalude is a replacement Prelude for Haskell, written for Advent of Code: Relude and about sixty libraries plus thirty modules of collections, grids, coordinates, parsing, search and Z3 helpers behind a dense Unicode notation, so a solution needs no imports. A guide with GHCi examples, the names real solutions use most, and a reference generated from the compiled library.

repos.name: ring-mods
repos.title: ring-mods research
repos.description: colmi r02 / r12 ring mods

repos.name: slick
repos.title: Slick — Slack reader
repos.description: A read-only Slack client for activity, conversations, threads and files. Slick for macOS and Android.

repos.name: stack
repos.title: stack — how I use computers (work in progress)
repos.description: Harry Askham's personal computing stack: one Nix flake, dozens of Android apps, and a swarm of agents. Work in progress.

repos.name: tendril
repos.title: Tendril · eyes and hands on a desktop, for agents
repos.description: Tendril is a stateless Rust CLI that lets agents see and drive desktops: list windows, displays and cameras, capture screenshots, read accessibility elements, type, click and scroll, on Linux, macOS, Windows and Android.

repos.name: tools
repos.title: Tools
repos.description: Tools: a physical-model synth and score language, a rhythm partner, speech synthesis and transcription, terminal handwriting and graphics, key lighting and release automation.
